widgets_values:
# Layers in, layers out

This demo round-trips a PSD's **actual layers** through the graph:

1. **Load PSD** reads your file and emits its real layer stack on the new
   **LAYERS** output — every layer's pixels, name, position, opacity, blend
   mode, and visibility. (The `psd` dropdown is empty until `ComfyUI/input/`
   has a file — click **Upload Photoshop File**, or queue
   `compose-layers-to-psd.json` once to make one.)
2. **Compose** writes that stack back out as a **real layered `.psd`** — same
   layer names, positions, opacity, blend modes, visibility — and, in *Wait
   for first save* mode, opens it in Photoshop and pauses the queue.
3. Edit in Photoshop, **save**, and your edit lands back in the graph in the
   top preview.

No Photoshop installed right now? Flip Compose's `mode` to **Don't open
(composite only)** — the layered file is still written into
`ComfyUI/input/` and both previews still work.

**`flatten_groups`** (Load PSD's last checkbox): off = every layer
individually in one flat list (group opacity/visibility applied to its
layers); on = each top-level group collapses to a single layer.

nodes.title: ComfyUI 0.31+ layer nodes & honesty notes
widgets_values:
# Using ComfyUI's own layer editor (0.31+)

On **ComfyUI 0.31.0 or newer** you can put core's layer nodes *between* the
two bridge nodes:

```
Load PSD ─LAYERS▶ Create Layered Image ─LAYERS▶ Compose ─▶ Photoshop
```

**Create Layered Image** opens a full-screen layer editor (move, rotate,
reorder, blend, opacity) — it needs the **Node 2.0** frontend mode; in
classic mode the widget shows "Compositor: Node 2.0 only". **Add Layer**
(core) appends one layer to a stack — different from this pack's
**Photoshop Add Layer**, which pushes a rendered image into the open
Photoshop document. Model nodes that output LAYERS (layer-splitting models)
wire straight into Compose the same way.

This file itself uses **only bridge nodes**, so it loads on any ComfyUI
version.

### Honesty notes
- ComfyUI composites blends/opacity in linear space; Photoshop in sRGB.
  Arrangement is identical; partially-transparent and non-normal-blend
  pixels render *close to*, not identical to, Photoshop. The written PSD in
  Photoshop is the authoritative render.
- The preview here flattens with plain alpha blending (blend modes not
  simulated). Text and smart-object layers arrive rasterized; adjustment
  layers are skipped.
- ComfyUI's compositor caps stacks at 50 layers; Compose has no such cap.
